notes: Named gates sharing this shape as of 2026-09-11: requireChannelAccess, requireReviewAccess, resolveStewardAuthority.

The shape's second half is intentionally a ready-to-return NextResponse ('response'), not a raw error string or code -- this is what lets every call site do 'if (!gate.ok) return gate.response;' with no per-route translation logic.
This is a code-shape convention, not a security or access-control claim -- it says how a gate REPORTS failure, not what it is permitted to gate.

canaries.assertion: resolveStewardAuthority's failure branch returns { ok: false, response } where response is a NextResponse, matching the sibling gates' shape.
Greps spine-aware routes/gates for shape drift; caught the original ad hoc '{ error }' shape before this fix.

statement: A new server-side caller-resolution gate in this codebase must return the established '{ ok: true, ...resolvedFields } | { ok: false, response: NextResponse }' shape (the shape requireChannelAccess and requireReviewAccess already use), never a bespoke failure shape a caller must separately translate into an HTTP response.

occurrences.defect: First written with an ad hoc '{ error: string }' failure shape, forcing a refactor of five route files plus two test canaries once tests/persona-spine-fetch.test.ts caught the drift from the established gate shape.
